issues.description: Tests substitute Addition(amount=0, puzzle_hash=zeros) sentinel to bypass __post_init__ instead of exercising real behavior
issues.detail: The test diff replaces additions=[] with additions=[Addition(amount=uint64(0), puzzle_hash=bytes32.zeros)] purely to satisfy CreateSignedTransaction.__post_init__'s len(additions) >= 1 requirement. This hides a real semantics question: either the legacy single-output path (amount + address + memos without an explicit Addition) still works and the test no longer verifies it, or zero-amount additions to the zero puzzle hash now leak into production transactions. Either restructure the test to reflect actual user intent, or have the validator/forwarder reject degenerate zero-amount/zero-puzzle-hash sentinels at the boundary. A test edit that exists only to placate the validator is hostile to the next maintainer and proves nothing about behavior.

issues.description: CreateSignedTransaction accreted CAT-specific fields (extra_delta, tail_reveal, tail_solution, puzzle_decorator), conflating distinct request types into a god-struct
issues.detail: CreateSignedTransaction was a generic 'create signed transaction' ADT. Bolting CAT-issuance and Clawback-decorator fields onto it so cat_spend can forward through it complects three concerns (generic transfer, CAT mint/melt, outgoing clawback) into one record. The invariant 'these fields are meaningful only for CAT spends' is unstated and unenforced; a non-CAT wallet with extra_delta set has undefined meaning. Prefer composition: a CatDiscrepancy value object (or sum/variant type) embedded alongside, and a shared private builder both endpoints call. The '# cat specific' comment is itself a confession that the data shape no longer matches the operation.

issues.description: cat_spend drops the explicit per-addition MAX_COIN_AMOUNT precondition check
issues.detail: The previous implementation iterated request.additions and raised ValueError(f'Coin amount cannot exceed {MAX_COIN_AMOUNT}') for each addition. The refactor forwards request.additions directly to create_signed_transaction without that check, and there is no visible evidence in the diff that the downstream path enforces the same bound on CAT additions. Either prove (with a comment pointer or a test) that the downstream path enforces the bound, or restore the explicit guard. A behavioral guarantee removed without a stated replacement is a silent contract change.

issues.description: send_transaction's 'Unexpected Address Prefix' error replaced by ensure_valid_address, silently changing the RPC error contract
issues.detail: Previously the endpoint raised ValueError('Unexpected Address Prefix') after a precise prefix comparison. The new code calls ensure_valid_address(..., allowed_types={AddressType.XCH}, config=self.service.config), which raises a different message and validates a different (though related) property. RPC clients commonly pattern-match on error strings; this change is API-observable. Either preserve the message, document the contract change in the PR description and a test, or revert. Don't change RPC error contracts inside a refactor PR.

issues.description: cat_discrepancy_validation duplicated as a property on two unrelated request types instead of composed as a shared value object
issues.detail: Both CATSpend.cat_discrepancy and CreateSignedTransaction.cat_discrepancy call the same free function over three loose Optional fields. The duplication has merely moved from the validation body to the field declarations and property wrappers. A CatDiscrepancy dataclass with (extra_delta: int, tail_reveal: Program, tail_solution: Program) and a from_optionals classmethod (or a small Protocol/mixin) would let the type system enforce the all-None-xor-none-None invariant once, eliminate the three type: ignore lines, and prevent the two classes from drifting apart when fields are added.

issues.description: Three type: ignore[arg-type] lines paper over a real type-narrowing problem that a different control-flow shape would eliminate
issues.detail: The condition 'None in {extra_delta, tail_reveal, tail_solution}' relies on set membership over a heterogeneous {str|None, bytes|None, bytes|None}, which mypy cannot narrow through. The fix is to rewrite as 'if extra_delta is None or tail_reveal is None or tail_solution is None: raise ...', which mypy does narrow, then assign to locals so the three type: ignore lines disappear. The comment 'Curious that mypy doesn't see the elif' was copied verbatim from the original and documents the author's surprise rather than the invariant. Encode the proof in the types.

issues.description: Discarded get_wallet call with '# opportunity to raise' comment is load-bearing dead-looking code
issues.detail: Both refactored endpoints call self.service.wallet_state_manager.get_wallet(...) purely for its raising side effect and discard the return value, while create_signed_transaction re-resolves the wallet internally. The '# opportunity to raise' comment is folklore in place of specification — a future maintainer will delete this line. Either extract a named validate_wallet_type(id, required_type) helper that states the precondition, pass the validated wallet through, or push the validation entirely into create_signed_transaction. Don't ship apology comments for code smells; fix the shape.

issues.description: json_serialize_for_transport round-trip is the wrong seam for an in-process call
issues.detail: send_transaction and cat_spend now build a typed CreateSignedTransaction, serialize it to a JSON transport dict, and hand the dict back to self.create_signed_transaction, which re-parses it. Same process, same memory, two serializations and one deserialization for a function call. The right shape is an internal _create_signed_transaction(request, action_scope, hold_lock) that takes the typed object directly; the three RPC handlers (send_transaction, cat_spend, create_signed_transaction) all call that helper. The current shape is easy (less code moved) but not simple — transport concerns are now intertwined with internal dispatch.

issues.description: Addition constructed with positional arguments at new call sites, fragile against field reordering
issues.detail: Throughout the refactor (send_transaction, cat_spend), Addition is built positionally: Addition(request.amount, decode_puzzle_hash(...), request.memos). Streamable dataclasses tend to grow fields and field order can change; positional construction breaks silently on reorder. Other call sites in the codebase use keyword arguments. Prefer Addition(amount=..., puzzle_hash=..., memos=...) at every new call site as a small enforceable rule that also documents intent at the call site.

issues.description: Patch bundles three independently-reviewable changes that should be three commits
issues.detail: The PR (1) extracts cat_discrepancy_validation as a shared helper, (2) extends CreateSignedTransaction with CAT fields plus puzzle_decorator, and (3) rewrites send_transaction and cat_spend to delegate. Bundling them hides that the third changes user-observable validation (address-prefix error became ensure_valid_address) and that fields like coin_announcements/puzzle_announcements/morph_bytes silently no-op on forwarded calls because the forwarders don't pass them. Split into three commits so each behavior change is reviewed on its own.

issues.description: puzzle_decorator typed as list[ClawbackPuzzleDecoratorOverride] with a 'slight hack' comment documenting that the type lies about the domain
issues.detail: The field carries the in-line comment 'Technically this value was meant to support many types here / However, only one is supported right now / as a slight hack, we'll specify that only Clawback is supported.' Either commit to the singular shape (ClawbackPuzzleDecoratorOverride | None — name it 'clawback override') or model the polymorphism honestly with a PuzzleDecoratorOverride base/Union so future widening isn't a breaking wire-format change. Apology comments without a tracking issue rot, and the type signature is what readers and clients will believe.

issues.description: extra_delta typed as str 'to support negative ints' — a pre-existing abstraction leak now propagated to a second request type
issues.detail: The field carries the comment '# str to support negative ints :(' — implementation seepage from a serializer limitation surfacing as a stringly-typed field on an otherwise-typed request object. Copying it unchanged from CATSpend into CreateSignedTransaction doubles the surface area of the leak. Either fix the serializer so the field can be a signed int, or introduce a small newtype (e.g., NegativeIntStr) that documents and validates the constraint at the boundary once.

issues.description: Address-to-puzzle-hash transformation inlined at two new call sites instead of named once
issues.detail: Both send_transaction and cat_spend now embed decode_puzzle_hash(ensure_valid_address(addr, allowed_types={AddressType.XCH}, config=self.service.config)) inside an Addition constructor argument. This is a small pure function asking to be named (xch_address_to_puzzle_hash(addr, config)). Inlining it twice complects 'validate this is an XCH address on this network' with 'build an Addition value', making both reading and future change harder than they need to be. Worth confirming there is a single canonical address-validation entry point in this file.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the refactor's direction is right — collapsing send_transaction and cat_spend onto create_signed_transaction is good special-case elimination — but the execution has structural and contract problems that must be fixed before landing. The two most serious issues are unanimous or near-unanimous: the test diff substitutes a zero-amount zero-puzzle-hash Addition sentinel to satisfy the new __post_init__ rather than exercising real behavior (testing the scaffold, not the code), and CreateSignedTransaction has been turned into a kitchen-sink request type by accreting CAT-specific and Clawback-decorator fields instead of composing a shared CatDiscrepancy value object and a shared internal builder. Several previously-explicit guarantees were silently changed or dropped (cat_spend's per-addition MAX_COIN_AMOUNT check, send_transaction's 'Unexpected Address Prefix' error message, validation now routed through ensure_valid_address with XCH-only allowed types) without being restated in code, comments, or tests. The forwarding seam round-trips through json_serialize_for_transport for an in-process call, the cat_discrepancy_validation helper carries three type: ignore lines and a duplicated property on two unrelated classes, and a discarded get_wallet call relies on an '# opportunity to raise' comment instead of a named precondition helper. The PR should be split into three commits, the typed forwarding path should bypass the JSON layer, the CAT-discrepancy fields should be composed (not duplicated), and the removed/changed validations should be either restored or explicitly documented and tested.
